statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-47268: ping in iputils before 20250602 allows a denial of service or incorrect statistics via a crafted ICMP Echo Reply, because of a signed 64-bit integer overflow in the round-trip-time calculation. Upstream fixed it in commit 070cfacd (https://github.com/iputils/iputils/commit/070cfacd7348386173231fb16fad4983d4e6ae40, iputils issue https://github.com/iputils/iputils/issues/584), which bounds tv_sec and tv_usec before computing the trip time in gather_statistics() in ping/ping_common.c. The Debian tracker lists trixie's 3:20240905-3 as vulnerable and the fix in 3:20250605-1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-47268). DHI iputils for Debian 13 rebuilds trixie's 3:20240905-3 with that upstream commit backported. The DHI Debian repository publishes one build of it, the fixed-version bound below (iputils-ping, iputils-tracepath, iputils-arping and iputils-clockdiff with their dbgsym packages, amd64 and arm64, checksums verified against the repository index). Its /usr/bin/ping on both architectures contains the two warnings the fix adds, "Warning: invalid tv_usec %ld us" and "Warning: invalid tv_sec %ld s", and the reworded "time of day goes back (%ld s)" message, and no longer contains the pre-fix "time of day goes back (%ldus)" form; its Debian changelog records the backport. The range ends at that build, the first and only one published, which carries the fix.
